text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The privatisation ministerial committee approved the sale of 40 percent of each of Egypt Aluminium Products/Alumisr and Sugar and Integrated Industries (SII), and 20 percent of Egyptian Iron and Steel. The sale also includes the whole equity of Upper Egypt Contracting.

- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi says the security bodies are monitoring closely all efforts by the banned Moslem Brotherhood to sow sectarian sedition. "We will not stop hitting at those who want to shake stability in order to take power," Alfi adds.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak is to meet Arab parliamentary speakers today and deliver an opening speech at their meeting tomorrow.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says the success of the tour of U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross depends on dealing with the Israeli settlement issue.
- Mubarak's political adviser, Osama el-Baz, says Ethiopia has not signed any agreement with Israel on water projects.
- An earthquake, registering 4.8 on the Richter scale, hits south Sinai yesterday morning. Officials said they did not receive any casualty or damage reports.
